newsitem.title: USA: Portland General sets power contracts.
newsitem.headline: Portland General sets power contracts.

text.p: Portland General Electric announced Friday agreements to supply wholesale electricity to Snohomoish County and Cowlitz County Public Utility Districts.
The contract with Snohomish is for five years; 50 megawatts the first year, increasing to 62 Mw in the fifth year. A one-year agreement with Cowlitz calls for the sale of 30 Mw.
In both cases, PGE responded to a request by the utilities for power suppliers to submit offers.

"We are pretty focused on being competitive," said Paul Koehler, manager of wholesale marketing at Portland General. He explained that by accessing the wholesale market through PGE, Snohomish can structure a price for their industrial customers based on the current wholesale price for electricity. In turn, Snohomish will receive a five-year commitment from industrial businesses to purchase electricity. In the case
of Cowlitz, the district is diversifying its power supply from Bonneville Power Administration and capitalizing on reduced power costs that they can pass on to all their customers.

Koehler said he does not expect to see many more long-term contracts in the Northwest since most of Bonneville's wholesale customers have either signed new 5-year deals with the federal power marketing agency or hooked up with other suppliers.
